main.format_help: Output format: rich (default), plain, or json.
main.config_help: Path to a split-config directory (containing config.json5 + overlays). Overrides ./config/ and $PERSONALSCRAPER_CONFIG. Must be placed BEFORE the subcommand.
main.invalid_format: Invalid --format '{{value}}'. Choose rich, plain, or json.

migrate_category.help:
Rewrite media_item.category_id for renamed categories.

Rewrites every ``media_item`` row whose ``category_id`` equals ``--from``
to ``--to``.  Run this after renaming a category in ``categories.json5``
to clear orphan-tagged rows shown by ``library status``.

The target ``--to`` must already be a declared category id in the current
config (the rename must be applied first).  The operation is idempotent.

Examples:
    personalscraper config migrate-category --from old_cat --to new_cat
migrate_category.to_help: New category_id to write (must be declared in config)
migrate_category.config_help: Path to config.json5 or config dir

init_config.help:
Create ./config/ from the config.example/ template directory.

Run without arguments for interactive mode (prompts for key values).
Use --yes to skip all prompts and accept defaults.
Use --dry-run to preview what would be created without writing anything.

Examples:
    personalscraper init-config
    personalscraper init-config --yes
    personalscraper init-config --output /custom/path/config --force
    personalscraper init-config --dry-run
init_config.example_help: Path to the example template directory to copy from.
init_config.output_help: Destination path for the new config directory.
init_config.yes_help: Skip interactive prompts and accept all defaults.
init_config.force_help: Overwrite output directory if it already exists.
init_config.dry_run_help: Preview mode: show what would be created without writing any files. Checks that config.example/ exists and reports the target path.
init_config.sync_help: Additive sync from config.example to canonical config (non-destructive).
init_config.canonical_not_found:
Error: canonical config directory not found: {{output}}
Set ${{env_var}} to point to your config directory, or pass --output explicitly to target a different location.
init_config.dry_run_exists: [DRY-RUN] WARNING: {{output}} already exists; use --force to overwrite.

info.help:
Display version, config paths, and disk status.

Output format respects the global ``--format`` flag
(e.g. ``personalscraper --format json info``).

Examples:
    personalscraper info
    personalscraper --format json info

providers.help:
Print per-provider circuit state snapshot from the ProviderRegistry.

Output: one line per configured provider, format:
    {{name}}  circuit={{state}}  failures={{failures}}

Exits non-zero if RegistryConfigError is raised during boot validation
(missing credentials or broken config).
providers.config_help: Override default config/providers.json5 for boot validation.

schedule.help:
Run a personalscraper command at every boundary of a cron expression, forever.

The job is everything after ``--``: ``personalscraper schedule --cron '15 * * * *' -- health-check``.
One run at a time, never started early, never cut by a second tick; stops on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Args:
    ctx: Typer context; its extra arguments are the job's CLI arguments.
    cron: The 5-field cron expression.

Raises:
    typer.Exit: Code 2 when the expression is malformed or no job follows ``--``.

torrents.no_client: No torrent client configured (set torrent.active in torrent.json5).
torrents.list_help:
List completed torrents from the active qBittorrent client.

Prints one line per completed torrent (state / progress / size /
seeding / name) and a summary count. Exits 2 with a friendly
message when the torrent client is unreachable (auth lockout, IP
ban, daemon down) so monitoring tools can branch on the exit
code. Used by the ``pipeline-monitor`` skill's GATE 0 inventory.

Output format respects the global ``--format`` flag.

watch.no_client: No active torrent client configured (config.torrent.active is empty).
watch.sentinel_consumed: Consumed by the watch daemon next cycle -> pipeline run with reason=manual; if the daemon is down the sentinel persists until next boot.
watch.help:
Start the watcher daemon (single-process scheduler).

Polls the configured torrent client each cycle, consults the
:class:`~personalscraper.acquire.watcher.WatcherService` decision engine,
and spawns ``personalscraper run --no-console`` (async, tracked) or
``personalscraper cross-seed --hash {{hash}}`` (sync, sequential) as
subprocesses.  The daemon itself does NOT acquire ``pipeline.lock``
(W6) — only its spawned children do.

Runs until SIGTERM, SIGINT, or a fatal error.
watch.now_help:
Write the sentinel file that the watcher daemon consumes next cycle.

No IPC, no daemon dependency — if the daemon is down, the sentinel is
consumed at next boot.  Same channel as the future Web UI (W4).

The running ``personalscraper watch`` daemon detects this file at the
next poll cycle and fires a pipeline run with ``reason=manual``.

supervise.help:
Start the supervisor: the one process that starts the asked pipeline runs and rescrapes.

Holds the environment's lease, starts the head of the queue in a detached worker when
nothing runs and pipeline.lock is free, settles each worker from its exit code or its
heartbeat, and runs the watcher's poll, whose automatic runs join the same queue.

Runs until SIGTERM or SIGINT; a clean stop releases the lease.
supervise.no_client: No active torrent client: the watcher is idle, asked runs are still started.

health_check.no_alert_help: Do not send the Telegram alert (check only).
health_check.help:
Check daemon liveness + recent log errors + stuck lock; alert on anomalies.

Exits 0 when healthy, 1 when any anomaly is found (Telegram alert sent unless
``--no-alert``). Intended to run under PM2 on an hourly cron.

Args:
    ctx: Typer context carrying the loaded config on ``ctx.obj``.
    lookback_minutes: Recent-error scan window.
    max_run_minutes: Held-lock age beyond which the pipeline is stuck.
    no_alert: Suppress the Telegram alert (still logs + exits non-zero).

opt.check: Run only the named check(s); repeatable
opt.no_post_maintenance: Skip automatic index maintenance after dispatch (scan/relink/fix).
opt.skip_trailers: Skip the trailers pipeline step for this invocation.
opt.continue_on_trailer_error: Do not abort dispatch when the trailers step crashes.
opt.headless: Run with no subscribers (silent mode for cron / CI). Disables Rich console output and Telegram notifications.
opt.no_console: Disable Rich console output (progress bars, live tables). Telegram notifications remain active. Used by the Watcher daemon (``personalscraper watch``) when spawning pipeline runs; contrast with ``--headless`` which disables both Rich and Telegram. If both are passed, ``--headless`` wins.

scrape.help: Scrape metadata and artwork from TMDB/TVDB.

verify.help:
Verify and qualify scraped media before dispatch.

The ``--list-checks`` listing and the unknown-``--check`` validation run
{{marker}}before{{marker}} any lock/journal scaffold — a pure listing or an argument error
must not take ``pipeline.lock`` nor write a ``pipeline_run`` row. Only once
the arguments are accepted does the real work run inside the shared
:func:`~personalscraper.cli_helpers.boundary` scaffold via
:func:`_verify_run`.

enforce.help:
Enforce staging conventions: sanitize filenames, validate structure, check coherence.

``--list-checks`` and the unknown-``--check`` validation run {{marker}}before{{marker}} the
lock/journal scaffold (they must not take ``pipeline.lock`` nor journal a
run); the accepted-argument path runs the real work inside the shared
:func:`~personalscraper.cli_helpers.boundary` scaffold via :func:`_enforce_run`.

clean.help:
Run reclean + dedup only (process sub-step, SH-21 / AR-C).

Standalone CLI surface around :func:`personalscraper.process.run.run_clean`.
Useful for debugging the clean sub-step in isolation and for composition
with other operator workflows (e.g. dry-run a clean pass before launching
the full process step). The full pipeline still invokes ``run_clean``
internally via ``run_process`` — this command does not alter that flow.

cleanup.help:
Run empty-directory cleanup only (process sub-step, SH-21 / AR-C).

Standalone CLI surface around :func:`personalscraper.process.run.run_cleanup`.
Removes empty directories left behind by previous steps. Distinct from
``clean`` (which performs reclean + dedup of polluted folder names); this
command only operates on empty directories. Useful for tidying staging
between manual operator interventions. The full pipeline still invokes
``run_cleanup`` internally via ``run_process`` — this command does not
alter that flow.

process.help: Run process phase only (reclean + dedup + scrape + cleanup).
